article.title: Why Good Decisions Depend on the Value of Information
article.why: 從決策門檻與期望值理解什麼資訊值得花成本取得，以及何時應停止分析。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Decision Theory

paragraphs.en:
Decision makers often respond to uncertainty by asking for more information. More research feels safer than acting with an incomplete picture. Yet information is not automatically valuable. A report can be accurate, interesting, and expensive while having almost no effect on the decision. The economic value of information depends on whether learning something new can change what you choose and improve the expected outcome enough to justify the cost of learning it.

Consider a company deciding whether to launch a product in a new market. Management estimates that demand could be high or low. If demand is high, launching creates substantial value; if demand is low, the launch destroys value. One option is to launch immediately. Another is to commission a market test, wait for the result, and then decide. The test has value only because it may lead the company to launch in one state of the world and not launch in another.

This idea can be formalized with expected value. First calculate the best decision using current information. Then imagine receiving additional information and being allowed to choose again after seeing it. The difference between those two expected outcomes is the value of that information before considering its cost. Perfect information gives an upper bound: no imperfect study, survey, pilot, or model should rationally cost more than the benefit you would obtain from knowing the uncertain state perfectly.

The framework produces an important result: uncertainty alone does not justify research. Suppose two possible market sizes are both large enough that launching is profitable. Even if you are highly uncertain about which size is correct, perfect information may have almost no decision value because the action does not change. You would launch either way. The information may improve the forecast, but it does not improve the choice.

The opposite can also happen. A relatively small amount of uncertainty can be extremely valuable when the decision sits near a threshold. If a project should be approved only when expected demand exceeds one million units, and your current estimate is close to that boundary, a modest improvement in information can frequently switch the recommended action. Information is especially valuable near decision boundaries because it has a greater chance of changing behavior.

Quality matters as well as quantity. Real studies are not perfect. A customer survey may be biased, an A/B test may measure only short-term behavior, and a predictive model may have classification errors. The relevant question is not whether the signal is flawless but how its error structure affects decisions. A noisy test can still be valuable if positive and negative results meaningfully update the probability of important states. Conversely, a sophisticated model can have little value if its predictions rarely change the action.

Timing is another part of the calculation. Information received after a contract deadline has no value for that decision. A six-month pilot may generate excellent evidence but sacrifice a market window. Waiting can also reveal information naturally without paying for a formal study, but delay itself may carry opportunity cost. Therefore the value of information should be compared with both the direct research cost and the cost of postponing action.

The concept also helps teams choose what to measure. Instead of asking, ‘What else would we like to know?’ ask, ‘Which unknowns could actually reverse or materially alter our decision?’ This question focuses analysis on consequential uncertainty. For a factory investment, demand elasticity and construction cost may matter greatly, while a more precise estimate of a minor administrative expense may not. For an AI deployment, false-positive cost, adoption, and failure modes may matter more than a marginal improvement in benchmark accuracy.

There is also a strategic dimension. Some experiments create options. A small pilot can generate information while limiting downside and preserving the ability to expand later. In such cases, the value comes from the combination of learning and reversibility. The organization pays a limited amount today to avoid committing fully before uncertainty resolves. This is one reason staged investment can outperform an all-or-nothing decision even when the staged approach appears slower.

Value-of-information thinking does not eliminate judgment. Probabilities and payoffs are often uncertain themselves, and political or organizational constraints may matter. But the framework disciplines the conversation. It separates curiosity from decision relevance and reminds analysts that the purpose of information is not merely to reduce uncertainty; it is to improve action.

Before commissioning another dashboard, survey, model, or consulting study, identify the decision, the available alternatives, and the threshold at which the preferred action changes. Then ask what new evidence could realistically move your belief across that threshold. If no plausible result would change the decision, additional information may still satisfy curiosity, but its decision value is low. If several plausible results would change the action, learning may be worth paying for. The most useful information is not necessarily the information that makes us most certain. It is the information that helps us choose differently when choosing differently matters.

This perspective can also prevent analysis paralysis. Teams often continue collecting evidence because uncertainty remains visible. A stopping rule based on decision value gives them a better question: has the remaining uncertainty become too small to justify another round of learning?
paragraphs.zh: 資訊並不因為能降低不確定性就自動有價值。真正的資訊價值來自它是否可能改變決策，並讓預期結果改善到足以補償取得資訊的成本。完美資訊可以視為價值上限：如果不論得到哪種結果都會做同一件事，那即使高度不確定，資訊的決策價值仍可能很低；反之，當估計值接近決策門檻時，小幅改善資訊就可能很有價值。還要同時計算研究成本、等待造成的機會成本，以及實驗訊號本身的錯誤。實務上應先問『哪些未知真的可能改變行動？』再決定要不要做更多分析。小型 pilot 之所以有價值，也在於它把學習與可逆性結合，保留之後擴張的選擇權。
paragraphs.ja: 情報は不確実性を減らすだけでは自動的に価値を持ちません。重要なのは、新しい情報が意思決定を変え、期待成果を情報取得コスト以上に改善できるかです。どの結果でも同じ行動を取るなら、予測精度が上がっても意思決定価値は低い一方、判断閾値の近くでは少しの情報が行動を変えるため価値が高まります。調査費だけでなく待つ機会費用や信号の誤差も考えます。追加分析の前に『どの未知が実際に行動を変え得るか』を明確にすると、analysis paralysisを避けやすくなります。

quiz.question: Why can perfect information have low value even under high uncertainty?
quiz.answer: Because the preferred action may be the same in every plausible state.

quiz.question: When is information especially valuable?
quiz.answer: When the current estimate is near a decision threshold and new evidence can change the action.

quiz.question: Output: Name one uncertainty that could change an AI deployment decision.
quiz.answer: Example: false-positive cost, user adoption, or the severity of a failure mode.
